chunk_findings.detail: The new guard only checks whether *any* finding is `confirmed`; it does not verify that the `stale` tree movement is the confirmed fix itself. Given a gate at budget cap with all findings triaged (`counts["untriaged"] == 0`), one confirmed finding (`counts["confirmed"] > 0`), and an unrelated commit that lands on the item after the last review, `stale` is non-empty because the current tree was not reviewed. Since `counts.get("confirmed")` is truthy, this line skips the stale protection, and the settle code below marks the gate passed even though the current tree contains unreviewed changes. The original guard existed precisely to prevent a pass when the reviewed tree is not the tree the item holds now.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:389

chunk_findings.detail: The mixed test is vacuous for the boundary it claims to protect. `_setup` generates every finding on the same `x.py:{n}` line, and the confirmed fix changes exactly that line (`x = 2  # fixed finding 1`). So the moved content for the refuted finding is the very text explained by the confirmed fix. An implementation of `_settle_after_cap` that merely checks “there is at least one confirmed finding, so ignore the stale tree for every refutation” would pass this test, even though it would incorrectly pass a gate when a refuted finding is on a different moved file/line whose change no confirmed fix explains. A correct regression test must move a file/line for the refuted finding independently of the confirmed fix and assert the gate still fails.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_round_budget.py: test_mixed_refuted_and_confirmed_settle_despite_the_fix_moving_the_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `counts.get("confirmed")` checks for the existence of *any* confirmed finding in the current round, but does not verify whether all findings from that stale round have been triaged. If a round produces multiple findings and only a subset are triaged as `confirmed` while others remain untriaged or are in different states, `counts.get("confirmed")` evaluates to truthy and bypasses the stale check, allowing a gate to settle prematurely before all findings are resolved.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard still does not tie `stale` to the confirmed fixes. If a gate is at its round cap and has one confirmed-and-fixed finding on `f1.py`, then after the fix an unrelated commit adds or changes `f2.py` (a file inside the same item), `stale` is non-empty because the current tree differs from the reviewed tree. With `counts == {"confirmed": 1, "untriaged": 0, "refuted": 0}`, the condition `not counts.get("confirmed") or counts.get("refuted")` is false, the stale protection is skipped, and `_settle_after_cap` settles the gate. The gate then passes over `f2.py` content no review ever saw. The bypass should require that the stale delta is exactly the confirmed fixes, not merely that no finding was refuted.

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard only checks whether *any* finding is `confirmed`; it does not verify that the `stale` tree movement is the confirmed fix itself. Given a gate at budget cap with all findings triaged (`counts["untriaged"] == 0`), one confirmed finding (`counts["confirmed"] > 0`), and an unrelated commit that lands on the item after the last review, `stale` is non-empty because the current tree was not reviewed. Since `counts.get("confirmed")` is truthy, this line skips the stale protection, and the settle code below marks the gate passed even though the current tree contains unreviewed changes. The original guard existed precisely to prevent a pass when the reviewed tree is not the tree the item holds now.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/triaging.py:389

chunk_findings.detail: The mixed test is vacuous for the boundary it claims to protect. `_setup` generates every finding on the same `x.py:{n}` line, and the confirmed fix changes exactly that line (`x = 2  # fixed finding 1`). So the moved content for the refuted finding is the very text explained by the confirmed fix. An implementation of `_settle_after_cap` that merely checks “there is at least one confirmed finding, so ignore the stale tree for every refutation” would pass this test, even though it would incorrectly pass a gate when a refuted finding is on a different moved file/line whose change no confirmed fix explains. A correct regression test must move a file/line for the refuted finding independently of the confirmed fix and assert the gate still fails.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_round_budget.py: test_mixed_refuted_and_confirmed_settle_despite_the_fix_moving_the_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `counts.get("confirmed")` checks for the existence of *any* confirmed finding in the current round, but does not verify whether all findings from that stale round have been triaged. If a round produces multiple findings and only a subset are triaged as `confirmed` while others remain untriaged or are in different states, `counts.get("confirmed")` evaluates to truthy and bypasses the stale check, allowing a gate to settle prematurely before all findings are resolved.
